issue.title: Thinking tags inside a save block silently prevent tool execution

steps:
In the current working directory, create a file named prompt_template.xml for our LLM evaluation harness. Its content must be exactly the following template (keep every tag and line as-is):

<system>
You are a careful math tutor.
</system>
<instructions>
Before answering, reason inside the thinking tags, then give only the final number inside the answer tags.
</instructions>
<thinking>
Work through the problem step by step here.
</thinking>
<answer>
Final numeric answer here.
</answer>
Please show me the exact current content of prompt_template.xml as it is on disk, so I can verify it was created correctly.
expected: A valid save block containing literal thinking tags executes and writes the requested content.
defect: A valid save tool block containing literal thinking tags is discarded, so the requested file is not created.

fault location.explanation: Thinking-tag removal scans the whole markdown before fence parsing and strips the prefix through the closing tag, including a save block opening fence when literal tags occur in its body.

Root cause: SOURCE-CONFIRMED. _extract_codeblocks strips everything through a closing thinking tag when an opening tag starts a line, without first checking whether the tag occurs inside the body of a save code fence. This removes the fence and prevents tool extraction. The archived ACP/deepseek-chat run series reports ten effective executions reproducing the missing-file result; original runs 03 and 08 were Docker startup failures and remain in the copied archive. ACP does not emit normal tool_call notifications on this path, so absence of those events alone is not evidence of a miss: network.jsonl and file-evidence are required. The archive records a reasoning-tag control that did write the file. No new execution or fixing-commit comparison was performed; fixed_in remains unknown.
